customData.tooltip: Two pages, and this is the whole navigation. Click through to the console.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The only place on this screen where a run is named at all — and the only candidate slot for the stale flag and for saying which run these numbers came from.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
The alert threshold on the console is **2.5%**. This tile says 2.4%.

So the number everyone looks at is one tenth of a point from firing an alert, and the tile has no way to say so.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
The one KPI with no unit and no scale. 62 out of what, and is 62 good?

It is also the only tile that dies quietly: if the news stream missed the Cutoff this is computed from Last-Good, and nothing here says so.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
Three cards, one per report. Clicking opens the reader over this page — you do not download a PDF to read it.

Three cards is also three *latest*. Last week's Brief is not on this screen.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Eight days old today, and it sits at the same size and weight as one published this morning. The date is the only thing distinguishing them.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The dashboard chrome stays. The reader covers the page, it does not replace it.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**This frame is a stub and I know it.** You told me people spend more time here than on the dashboard, and it is the surface I have the least detail on.

What I have drawn is the minimum a reader must have: which report, which run produced it, its sections, and the way out. Everything else is a guess waiting to be corrected.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
My invention. A published report is frozen, so it is the one place in the product where 'which run made this' can be stated permanently and truthfully.

If this line does not exist today, a reader has no way to know whether what they are reading came from a degraded morning.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The escape hatch, not the main path — you download to *send* it to someone, not to read it.
